Simulate probability and contaminated non-probability samples

Source: R/simulate.R
simulate_mixture_data.Rd

Generates example data with a known data-generating process for demonstrations, tests and simulation studies.

Usage

simulate_mixture_data(
  family = c("gaussian", "binomial", "poisson"),
  n_prob = 200,
  n_nonprob = 200,
  contamination = 0.25,
  beta = NULL,
  sigma = 1,
  bad_beta = NULL,
  x_shift = 0,
  outcome_shift = 0,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

family

"gaussian", "binomial" or "poisson".

n_prob, n_nonprob

Sample sizes.

contamination

Fraction of contaminated NP units, in [0, 1].

beta

True target coefficients (intercept first). Defaults: c(2, 5) (Gaussian), c(0.2, 1, -0.8) (binomial), c(1.2, 0.5, -0.4) (Poisson).

sigma

Error standard deviation (Gaussian only).

bad_beta

Coefficients of the contaminating mechanism. Default: the intercept of beta with all slopes sign-flipped.

x_shift

Mean shift of contaminated units' covariates.

outcome_shift

Constant added to contaminated units' linear predictor.

seed

Optional seed (the global RNG state is restored afterwards).

Value

A list with data frames prob (columns y, x1, ...) and nonprob (same columns plus contaminated, 1 for contaminated units), and the list truth of generating values.

Details

Covariates \(x_1, \dots, x_{k}\) (\(k\) = length(beta) - 1) are independent standard normal in the probability sample and in the compatible part of the non-probability sample. Exactly round(contamination * n_nonprob) NP units are contaminated: their covariates are drawn from \(N(x_{shift}, 1)\) and their outcomes from the same family with linear predictor \(x'\beta_{bad} + \delta\) (bad_beta, outcome_shift). NP rows are randomly permuted.

Examples

d <- simulate_mixture_data("poisson", n_prob = 50, n_nonprob = 40,
                           contamination = 0.25, seed = 1)
str(d$nonprob)
#> 'data.frame':	40 obs. of  4 variables:
#>  $ y           : int  1 1 2 1 1 1 1 4 2 1 ...
#>  $ x1          : num  0.0174 1.5866 -0.6817 -1.1159 -0.3309 ...
#>  $ x2          : num  2.075 -0.4 -1.384 -0.334 -1.37 ...
#>  $ contaminated: int  0 1 0 0 1 0 0 0 1 0 ...
table(d$nonprob$contaminated)
#> 
#>  0  1 
#> 30 10
